concept.name: Vectorized backtest
concept.definition: A backtest that computes signals, positions, and returns primarily as aligned array operations rather than replaying individual events.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Construct lagged positions and return series, align them explicitly, and apply turnover and cost adjustments across the arrays.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: Daily signal s at row t is shifted one row before multiplying return r at t, preventing same-close look-ahead.
